title: Human reviewers missed one in three risky agent commands
friendlyTitle: People missed many dangerous AI agent requests
summary: Across more than 40,000 runs of a browser-based agent-permission game, players missed one in three threats on average. Familiar-looking npm scripts were a particular blind spot, and only about one in five players caught every threat without heavily blocking safe commands.
friendlySummary: In a game with more than 40,000 runs, people allowed about one in three dangerous commands. Normal-looking software commands were easy to trust by mistake.
whyItMatters: Approval prompts are not a complete security boundary: repetition, time pressure and missing context wear reviewers down. Run agents inside narrow sandboxes, limit secrets and permissions, and reserve human approval for clear high-risk transitions.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Do not depend only on “allow” buttons. Give AI agents limited access and keep private keys and important files outside their workspace.
